snippet.textDisplay:
Thank you, Julie, for your videos. I just wish I knew some of what you have been teaching us Before my father needed to live with us.
My father came to live with us after a small stroke left him no longer able to live by himself.
I knew he wanted to "go." He had just turned 90, he was no longer able to walk on his own, he was tired and I knew he was wanting to leave. So we explored the opportunity of "voluntary stopping eating and drinking". Online reading convinced us that refusing food and drink was Not suicide. So he tried it for a couple of days and thirst got the better of him, but at the same time he pretty much lost his appetite for any food, so he did die naturally anyway, however, it gave him comfort and the Power over his own life, that he Could refuse anymore sustenance in order to end his suffering on his terms. Miss you Dad. 😢

snippet.textDisplay: I have been caring for a lady for nearly 3 years. She has Parkinson's Disease and Parkinson's Dementia.  I swear she hates me, she just can't articulate.  I care for her the best I know how but it's really disheartening as she gives microagressions all the time.  It's so discouraging that I want to quit, but she's very close to dying and the family appreciates my help.  Ugh.  I dread going to work, even though I have been a caregiver for 15 years.  This is the first client that I sense does not like me.  I have told the coordinator and the other caregivers (we have a team) and they all roll their eyes and laugh.  Sigh

snippet.textDisplay: I am an 80 year old man with heart failure on in-home hospice with twice a week visits by RN.  My Caregiver is former CNA wife of 58 years who is, you guessed it, also 80.  Do you have a video on do's and don'ts of being the patient?
snippet.textOriginal: I am an 80 year old man with heart failure on in-home hospice with twice a week visits by RN.  My Caregiver is former CNA wife of 58 years who is, you guessed it, also 80.  Do you have a video on do's and don'ts of being the patient?

snippet.textDisplay:
Hey there♥️ Just my humble thoughts and opinions here but… start out by being yourself. Be honest with your partner about how you are feeling- even if it’s something that is difficult for you to say. You’ve been together for a long time and your partner deserves to hear from you about how you’re TRULY feeling- even IF it’s not great. This applies with speaking with your Dr’s too. If you’re feeling depressed they need to know. There IS help out there and support for you AND your partner. And there may be things you might not be able to speak with her about just yet or maybe even ever. But you may need SOMEONE to talk with about it- and professional, confidential support IS out there!!!
Be kind to yourself!!! You’re going through something major!! And it’s NOT easy!! Mentally, physically, emotionally or spiritually!!! You can’t right all the perceived wrongs you’ve done in your past. You can’t make amends for everything you’ve think you’re done wrong. And you’ll make yourself crazy trying to think of ways to fix it and do just that!!! If you ARE spiritual you’ll know what to do. If not then you can try to reach out to people who you wish to reach out to and do what you can- in sincerity WITHOUT mentioning your illness. It’s about your righting a wrong for the right reason- NOT because your time here is limited. It’s about fixing hearts and relationships period. If they aren’t interested or reject this olive branch. That’s ok. You’ve done your best for the right reasons.

About being a good patient? Just be a good person. When you’re sick, nurses understand you’re not always going to be all happy-go-lucky and cheerful!! Just be yourself hun.
And if you’re at home, just be yourself there too.
Don’t worry so much about what others think!! Just focus on you and your wife and family!!!! Do things that make you both feel happy!!! That creates memories together!!!

Not sure if this is what you were looking for 🤷🏻‍♀️ but I hope it helps!!!♥️🙏🏻♥️

Sending you my sincerest best wishes to you and your wife and family!!!

Michelle~
Retired Psychogeriatric Nurse

snippet.textDisplay: Just want to remind you about the most most important decision we need to make before we die, and that is to receive Jesus as our Lord and Savior. I just wanted to let you know a little about what the bible says. It takes more than just believing in God. John 3:3 says, we must be Born Again to get to heaven before our time is up.. Everyone has sinned and fallen short of God's glorious standard, and all need to be made right with God by his grace, which is a free gift. We need to be made free from sin through Jesus Christ. Bible also says, its not by works should any one boast. So being a good person does not get you to heaven either. The only way to heaven is by repenting of your sins, which means a change of mind, and putting your faith and trust in Jesus. Romans 10:13 says, Whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. So you see, there is a need for salvation to get to heaven. That is why Jesus died on the cross. He took all of our sins upon him, so that if you accept Him as your Lord and Savior, you can have eternal life in paradise. You do not get there being a good person, or doing good deeds. Many people believe that is all it takes. Jesus also says, that I am the way, the Truth, and the Life, no one comes unto the father, except through me. So please make that decision, so that you can have peace and comfort before your time is up. Its the most important decision of your life. You can then have that peace and assurance of salvation in your heart. All you have to do is humble your heart and pray with faith,... "I repent of my sins, and I turn to You. You said in Your word that if we confess with our mouth the Lord Jesus, and believe in our hearts that God raised Him from the dead, we shall be saved. I ask You Jesus to forgive me of all my sins, come into my heart, and take control of my life. From this day forward I want to live for you. ..... It's not about the words, it's about your heart. The Lord will then send His Holy Spirit to live on the inside of you. The Holy Spirit is Gods seal of salvation, and your evidence you have been Born Again. He will transform your heart and mind. He will bring you into a personal relationship with Jesus. You will become a new person inside. 2 Corinthians 5:17 says: “Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new”. Its truly amazing! You will be filled with peace, love, and joy of the Lord inside you. All the fruits of the Holy Spirit. He will comfort you in your time of need, and give you the strength to endure. No matter what you are going through, Jesus wants to help you through it. You can lean on Him. Its the most important decision of anyone's life. God's Word says that we are saved by grace through faith in Christ Jesus and not by our own efforts or works (Ephesians 2:8-9). Grace Alone. Jesus is the only way to heaven. Please believe me, its all in the bible. Its the Word of God..I am not judging or condemning anyone, just letting you know there is much more if you put your trust in Him. Jesus cares for you, and does not wish for you to be separated from him. Please don't wait. Today is the day of salvation. He loves you, and does wish for anyone to be apart from Him, but to have eternal life in heaven. I'm praying for you. Please ask Jesus to come into your life today, my friend, You are special to Jesus. Romans 10:9-10. "If thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. Be blessed

snippet.textDisplay: I’m a caregiver for my husband who has dementia & doesn’t want to eat anything. He will try to drink juices, but doesn’t usually succeed. What to do?
snippet.textOriginal: I’m a caregiver for my husband who has dementia & doesn’t want to eat anything. He will try to drink juices, but doesn’t usually succeed. What to do?

snippet.textDisplay: Try soft foods, i.e. pureed.  Do you have a blender or food processor?  Take his favorite food, say . . BBQ chicken, or whatever, and puree it.  After blending, add warm water if it needs to be creamier, and blend again.  Try spooning a half teaspoon at a time.  His liquids may need to be thickened.  There is a product that you add to liquids that makes it thicker and slower going down.  Demented people will refuse food and drink if they know they will choke.

snippet.textDisplay: I'm being with my 82-year-old stepmom for 11 years now, she is down to 91 lb she cannot eat anything without choking, and I'm scared to death that she's going to aspirate, I think she needs a feeding tube is what some of the doctors are telling me, and I also told me to check on palliative care, to help out with these things at home that she needs, my daughter aspirated in the hospital, and ended up with aspiration pneumonia, and she passed away the next day and ICU, I don't want this to happen to my stepmom, and I cannot let her lay here and starve to death, I think palliative care would be great for her, we see the heart doctor tomorrow, and then we see a new ENT FOR A SECOND OPINION, her PC doctor said that he really wants a second opinion and I'm glad he does, the one we sing the last year when I asked him when he wanted her to come back he said I don't, he said there's nothing I can do for her, he said you need to think about what you're going to do, he said she'll either end up on a feeding tube, or she's going to end up with aspiration pneumonia and pass away, so we're hoping that tomorrow they can tell us that they may can open her throat up so that she can eat, she's going so long now without eating that she's very very weak, she can hardly stand up, and this is killing me seeing her that way, she was always a tough tough woman, I've seen her work three jobs when we were kids just to help raised 5 kids, and only two of the kids were hers, but she was really good to us other three, that her step kids, she tells me like 10 times a day on text that she loves me, she's always said she loves me and the other kids too but she's doing it a whole lot and that scares me too, I've lost my daughter and my mama my daddy and my husband, and they were all sudden deaths, I have never taken care of someone and watching them decline, it's really hard, I know that I'm already grieving, what's going to happen eventually, and it's a different kind of grief, I never got over grieving for my daughter or my mom or my husband, I think when you love someone that much you will always grieve, what keeps me going is knowing I will see them again one snippet.textDisplay: My mother at 97 years, 320 days, was resuscitated by the EMTs, despite a DNR order. snippet.textDisplay:
I just wanted to say thank you Julie, you answered some of my questions in other videos about those who pass away from renal failure. My husband had kidney disease and due to another medical problem that he developed 14 years prior, he couldn't do dialysis. He passed away today June 9, 2024. He was 61 years young, but had many health problems. I already miss him dearly ... it has been a whirlwind of emotions today, and tomorrow we deal with the funeral home...

Before he passed away, we listened to some music, one of the songs was the one we played at our wedding "I will be there" by Steven Curtis Chapman, our 25th wedding anniversary is June 12th, 3 days away. We listened to Amazing Grace by Peter Hollins and Home Free, it was one of his favorites, and said he wanted it played at his funeral, I wanted him to hear it and other songs one last time. We shared family memories with his nurse, had some laughs about the fun we had as a family as we watched and listened to him take his last breath... he will truly be missed! On the way home, I turned on the radio to hear one of his favorite songs... "Every breath you take... I will be watching you" by the band The Police, perhaps it was his way of saying he will be watching over me... and our family.

To those of you reading this... remember that tomorrow is never promised, for the old or the young! Spend time with those you love... put down your phones, your games, and any differences you may have or had, life is too precious to be distracted by THINGS that really don't matter!! Share some love today with someone who misses you, but you will miss once they are gone and you wished you had made more time for them! Spread some love... isn't that what our world truly needs right now?!! ❤❤❤

snippet.textDisplay: I'm so aggravated that my sister's palliative team didn't call in hospice sooner. She started getting where she wouldn't eat 5 months ago. Every time she did she'd throw up. She became unsteady on her feet, speech slurring, out of breath easy. Shes been fighting cancer for 15 years, metastatic breast cancer that went to her lung and months ago to her brain. She did a few chemo treatments, stopped to see if it helped. She got an infection in her port, had it removed and eventually put back in but all the while she kept getting worse. She couldn't walk more than 10 feet and her palliative dr told her not give up yet, she needed to regain strength by eating 🙄. I KNEW she was slowly dying. A month went by before her dr saw her again and finally said she needed hospice. That was over a week ago. So here is my sister finally in a bed at home, under 100 pounds, unable to eat or barely swallow, unable to sit up on her own. And hospice comes only twice a week. They finally prescribed her morphine in syringe form so we can squirt in her mouth. And they were shipping mouth swabs. Thank God for our sister in law who worked as a home health provider for many years and just retired. She does have some knowledge on what to do.

snippet.textDisplay: What about bathing? It sure was stressed by hospice for my mom but she was very resistant. As I was her sole caregiver most of the time I didn’t bother. Earlier on my sister could get her to bathe but the sister wasn’t around all time. My mom didnt smell bad so I wasn’t too concerned. (Later on she did become incontinent so we had to clean her that way and she didn’t like it!) My understanding is, especially, dementia patients are resistant to bathing (my mom had mid-stage dementia). She died age 95, peacefully on her couch at home with us present, on the same day our dad died 9 years earlier.
